description: Independent English C1 film-review comprehension bank requiring human pedagogical approval.

tabs.title: Evaluation
tabs.description: Apply the ideas to new situations.

questions.q: Why does the reviewer distinguish knowing what to feel from knowing what to do?
choices: The film's opening is too abstract for the audience to understand.
The camera wrongly presents a wrapper as an actual rare animal.
Moving images can make a problem vivid without explaining a workable response.
The reviewer believes emotional responses have no place in documentaries.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 1 of this C1 film criticism develops the stated argument; the competing interpretations omit or exaggerate relevant conditions.

questions.q: What makes the elegant images of the night cleaners 'double-edged'?
choices: They suggest that cleaners are uninterested in environmental questions.
They honour the work visually while keeping the workers' conditions and influence obscure.
They prove that the square is always clean during the day.
They establish that beautiful images cannot contain any argument.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 2 of this C1 film criticism develops the stated argument; the competing interpretations omit or exaggerate relevant conditions.

questions.q: Why is the cleaner's remark about five in the morning arguably political?
choices: It is an explicit request for the director to support a political party.
It demonstrates that the square is most polluted at dawn.
It shows the cleaner intends to leave the job immediately.
It draws attention to essential work that goes unseen by most beneficiaries.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 3 of this C1 film criticism develops the stated argument; the competing interpretations omit or exaggerate relevant conditions.

questions.q: Why is the council manager's interview especially revealing?
choices: It presents real constraints without denying the desirability of change.
It demonstrates that the council has already rejected every deposit scheme.
It confirms that washing equipment is the only factor to consider.
It shows the manager has complete control over all local waste policy.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 4 of this C1 film criticism develops the stated argument; the competing interpretations omit or exaggerate relevant conditions.

questions.q: What is the effect of repeating the image of a teenager dropping a bottle?
choices: It makes the costs of the return system more transparent.
It proves that no adult has ever discarded a bottle.
It shifts attention from systemic design towards an individual who can be blamed.
It encourages the audience to compare different cleaning shifts.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 5 of this C1 film criticism develops the stated argument; the competing interpretations omit or exaggerate relevant conditions.

questions.q: Why is the distinction between named people and silhouettes an ethical issue for the reviewer?
choices: It affects whose perspective is recognised as part of the film's argument.
It shows the producer could not afford additional cameras.
The documentary is required by law to name every participant.
It proves the manager was more important than the cleaners in every way.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 6 of this C1 film criticism develops the stated argument; the competing interpretations omit or exaggerate relevant conditions.

questions.q: Why does the volunteer's admission after the credits make the proposed system more credible?
choices: It proves the volunteers had hidden all their mistakes from the audience.
It invites revision after acknowledging an unexpected practical cost.
It makes the film's opening sequence factually impossible.
It means no reusable container could ever be efficient.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 7 of this C1 film criticism develops the stated argument; the competing interpretations omit or exaggerate relevant conditions.

questions.q: A film praises reusable cups but never mentions collection or washing. Which improvement would the reviewer prefer?
choices: Replace the entire film with a technical spreadsheet.
Remove interviews with anyone who might disagree.
Include a second dramatic shot of a careless consumer.
Let the audience see both the appealing goal and the practical work that supports it.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 4 of this C1 film criticism develops the stated argument; the competing interpretations omit or exaggerate relevant conditions.

questions.q: Why does the writer say a documentary should not resemble a council report?
choices: Detailed evidence is incompatible with visual storytelling.
Artistic rhythm and character are valuable, although framing choices still carry implications.
Any discussion of budgets necessarily spoils a documentary.
The reviewer rejects the value of public institutions.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 6 of this C1 film criticism develops the stated argument; the competing interpretations omit or exaggerate relevant conditions.

questions.q: Which possible final scene would best address the film's missed opportunity?
choices: A longer view of an empty square without workers.
A celebrity praising everyone who used a reusable cup.
A scene that blames the public without explaining any alternative.
A discussion of the project's costs, problems and next adjustments.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 7 of this C1 film criticism develops the stated argument; the competing interpretations omit or exaggerate relevant conditions.
